note: Written by us, synthetic (09 §18.3). Three prompts per stratum for the pilot (flow.md F8). Paste-in prompts are an instruction, a blank line, then the text (P6 decision 10). Echo prompts (correct-korean, defective-korean) ask for the text back unchanged, so the reply carries text whose zones and defects we wrote; their `zones` list what the exclusion pass must find in the reply.

strata.conversation: short Korean questions: ordinary replies, the usable floor, reply length
strata.coding-reply: explain or review code, no edits: coding.06/07 pressure, Latin identifiers in Korean prose
strata.coding-edit: edits in the fixture project: task_type coding, artifacts outside the reply
strata.document: Korean prose written to a .md file: task_type document, the reply-only measurement limit
strata.delegation: delegation to a shipped agent: agent layer, coding.19, the hand-back capture
strata.correct-korean: deliberately correct Korean, echoed: false-positive rates
strata.defective-korean: deliberately defective Korean, echoed: detection on known defects
strata.english: English prompts: instruction_lang covariate; the policy must not force translation

gaps: No multi-turn conversation beyond arm C's two turns: long-session drift is not sampled.
No prompt makes the model read Korean text from a file and rewrite it there: that pair never enters a record (09 §14.3), so Tier 2 is sampled only by paste-in.
The fixture project is one small Python package: other languages and large repositories are not sampled.
No prompt asks for a formal report as an attached document other than the three document prompts.
Echo strata measure the pass and the measurements on text the model copies; the model may still alter it, and a reply that does not reproduce a labelled span is counted apart.
English prompts are three and all technical or workplace; English chit-chat is not sampled.
